title: Robo-Catcher
description: A softball machine that catches an incoming throw and returns it, built by a 12 person capstone team for under $700. I owned the electronics and firmware.
og_alt: Render of the Robo-Catcher softball catch and return machine.
lede: A machine that catches the ball and returns it. Our capstone team built it for under $700.

brief.label: Role
brief.value: Feeding subsystem co-lead, all electronics and firmware

brief.label: Build
brief.value: Laser cut HDF and 3D printed parts

sections.label: The feeder
paras: The feeder is a rotating dual chamber: catch a ball, rotate 180 degrees, hand it to the return flywheel.
One ESP32 runs everything. A wireless remote starts and stops it.

frames.alt: The team running the machine on the field
frames.caption: On the field

list: 100% feed indexing on competition day: every ball delivered, no misses
Under $700 total build cost against a $700 cap
55 lb, one person portable, assembles with no tools
1.5 hours continuous runtime on a single 12 V 20 Ah SLA battery

frames.alt: The finished machine on the field
frames.caption: The finished machine

paras: The MATLAB torque study felt slow while teammates were already printing parts. Then the feeder ran a full competition day without a missed index.
